Power sharing rather than centripetal design explains Indian stability.
Asymmetric federalism as the core of multinational democracy.
Explains the Congress party's strength by its independence-era origins.
Party weakness, not security threats alone, explains military rule in Pakistan.
Reserved seats are a group-representation device.
Patronage democracy channels clientelism through ethnic head counts.
Ethnic parties need not outbid toward instability.
Quotas and ethnic parties are both routes to lower-caste representation.
Generalizes the fluidity of ethnic identity.
Electoral incentives, not civic ties, decide whether riots happen.
Both use electoral logic in ethnically divided democracies.
A majoritarian project against power sharing and secularism.
Elite parties win poor voters without coethnic patronage.
Hindu nationalist affiliates mobilize poor voters through services.
Formalizes the role of intermediaries in patronage.
Coercion and state resources, not reciprocal ties, sustain local power.
Oligarchic wealth and local bosses capture the state together.
Oligarchs capture decentralized local power.
Party collusion rather than oligarchic wealth explains weak accountability.
Adds embeddedness and state types to the developmental state.
Explains where cohesive developmental states come from.
Threats from contention build strong states and regimes.
Ruling parties are products of elite protection pacts, not independent causes.
Institutionalized parties rather than militaries sustain authoritarian rule.
Organizational power explains competitive authoritarian stability.
Palace networks, not the bureaucratic-military polity, run Thailand.
Electoral populism challenges palace-centered rule.
Populist mobilization often serves oligarchic interests.
Elected populists push regimes toward competitive authoritarianism.
Control, not grievance, explains violence in civil war.
Organization and control jointly shape insurgent behavior.
State-led Islamization versus civil Islamic pluralism.
Military rulers in Pakistan used Islamization to build state power.
Norms and identity rather than balancing explain ASEAN.
Small states hedge rather than balance.
Hedging works through regional institutions and norms.
